findings.title: Raw signup body, including plaintext password, is logged
findings.explanation: The log line writes the entire req.body before validation. That body contains the plaintext password, and the logger's redaction is not a safe guarantee here. Redaction is typically key-based, so it will miss misspelled or differently named fields (e.g. 'passwd', 'pass', 'Password' in a different case, nested objects), which are exactly the malformed payloads this change is meant to capture. Failed signups are the case most likely to carry unexpected shapes, so secrets can leak into logs, log aggregators, and backups. Instead, log only a safe summary: the list of keys received, the types of values, and the zod validation errors (without values), and never log the raw body.

findings.title: PII (email, organization) logged at info level for every signup attempt
findings.explanation: Even with passwords redacted, email addresses and organization names are personal data. Logging them for every attempt, including successful ones, at info level raises GDPR/privacy and retention concerns and may violate data handling policy. Log only what is needed for debugging, and only on failure. Consider masking the email (e.g. domain only) or hashing it.

findings.title: Logging is placed before validation and runs for every request, with an unbounded payload
findings.explanation: req.body is attacker controlled and can be large or deeply nested, which allows log flooding, inflated log costs, and log injection. The log also happens for all requests rather than just failures. Move the logging into the failure path by using safeParse (or catching ZodError) and log only the validation issues, field names and sizes/types, truncating where needed.

findings.title: Validation failure is not handled, so the real problem is not surfaced
findings.explanation: signupSchema.parse throws on invalid input, so the failure cause is not logged or returned in a structured way. Use safeParse, log error.issues (paths and codes, not values), and return a 400 with a clear error. That directly solves the stated debugging need without logging the payload. Also confirm that Express async error handling is in place, since a thrown error in an async handler may not reach the error middleware in Express 4.

findings.title: No test or verification of the redaction claim
findings.explanation: The description says the logger already redacts sensitive fields, but there is no test or reference showing which keys are covered. Add a test, or link to the redaction config, that shows password-like fields are masked for this route. If the logging remains, make it temporary and add a ticket to remove it.
